# P14 — the gather, and 128k prefills at PLACEHOLDER tok/s

> **PLACEHOLDER headline.**

## Where P13 left it

P13 closed the arithmetic and named the route. At 128 000 cells, ubatch 2048,
48 layers (ms a token):

	floor (everything flat in depth)   0.803
	attn.attn                          0.566
	attn.select                        0.233
	attn.score                         0.078
	attn.expand                        0.051
	                                 = 1.731, and 563.6 on the clock

900 tok/s is 1.111. P13's own summary of what that needed was three things —
the selection change, a wider ubatch, and the gather — and priced the gather at
2.8x on `attn.attn` from a union of "~4 574 cells" against the 14 976 the
16-cell rung reads.

**Both of those cell counts were wrong**, which is the first thing P14
measured. `AttnGPU.SelUnion` prices the question directly, on the selection a
pass actually left behind, and at 128 000 cells a sixteen-row query tile reads
**15 145 cells** where its rows' union holds **7 049** and one row selects
2 051. So the gather is worth **2.15x**, not 3.3x; the union is 3.4x one row's
reach, not 2.2x. That shortfall is why P14 is four changes and not two.

## P14-1: the selection over block scores, and the expansion is deleted

`llm_attn_select.comp` radix-selects over `llm_attn_expand.comp`'s tensor: one
f32 a cache cell a token, `rows * nKV` of them, which at 128 000 cells and a
2048-row batch is **1.14 GB of arena** and five streams of it per token — four
radix passes and the emit.

That tensor has `nKV/ratio + 1` distinct values in it. All `ratio` cells of a
pooled block carry one block score (`llm_attn_score.comp`) and every cell the
causal mask drops carries -inf, so the select can run over the **block** scores
with a per-block **weight** — how many of its cells this token can see, which is
closed form — and reach the same threshold, the same ties and the same bitmask.
`ratio` is 4 here, so that is a quarter of the traffic and the expansion is then
not computed at all.

`shaders/llm_attn_selblk.comp` is that kernel. Three things have to hold and all
three are arithmetic rather than hope:

1. **The threshold.** A weighted histogram over blocks counts exactly the cells
   the per-cell histogram counted, because every cell of block `b` has key `b`
   and nothing else does. The total weight is exactly `ncols`.
2. **The tie fill.** The reference appends cells equal to the threshold in
   ascending *cell* index (L4a), and the emit still walks cells ascending — it is
   the keys that come from blocks. Two blocks whose scores happen to be equal are
   one histogram bucket and two runs in the emit, and the emit takes the lower
   run first, as the per-cell code did.
3. **The dead cells.** Everything past this token's position is -inf, whose key
   `0x007FFFFF` is the smallest there is, and they are all *after* the live
   cells — so they enter as one weighted entry and fill from the lowest index.
   No block can collide with that key: the only bias that makes one -inf is the
   `b >= nBid` arm, and those blocks have weight zero.

The emit is still the one pass per cell, because the output is — but it is no
longer a read per cell. Cells are grouped `ratio` to a block and a word is
`32/ratio` blocks, so the key is fetched when the block changes; and a word
wholly past this token's position is every cell -inf with no read at all.

Measured — 4 layers, one full-attention layer, `-pp 2048 -ctx 136000`, scaled to
the 48 layers that count, with `attn.attn` and `attn.score` as the controls:

| ms a token at 128 000 | cell select | block select | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `attn.select` | 0.2808 | **0.0204** | **13.8x** |
| `attn.expand` | 0.0456 | — | gone |
| `attn.attn` (control) | 0.9516 | 0.9528 | 1.00x |
| `attn.score` (control) | 0.0792 | 0.0804 | 1.00x |

**13.8x and not the 4x the traffic argument predicts**, because two other things
went with it: the histogram is bounded at the last block a cell can reach, so a
shallow cache never visits the rest of the table, and the 16 KB of LDS that used
to cache 4 096 *cells* now caches 4 096 *blocks*, which is 16 384 cells.

`TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect` is the gate and it is an equality —
30 405 462 selected cells over four chunk schedules, and the layer's own output,
identical to the last bit. The schedules are the point: at 4096 tokens in a
4096-cell cache the whole cache is whole blocks, so `nBid >= nBlocks` and the
*incomplete tail* never exists; a run in chunks of seven reaches a cell count
that is not a multiple of `ratio` at every step, which is where the tail block's
weight and the causal boundary inside a partly visible block are both live.

The old kernel stays as the control arm (`LLM_ATTN_EXPAND_CELLS=1`), which is
also what `Cells()` needs — and the arena is allocated only on that arm, because
that is the point.

P13 compacted the *blocks* the selection leaves anything in and measured 1.00x.
The kernel it fed still read every cell of a live block, and the 2.15x between
15 145 and 7 049 is what a block list cannot reach: the granularity a
cooperative-matrix tile can skip at is sixteen cells and the selection's runs are
four.

So the list is per cell. `shaders/llm_attn_gather.comp` emits, per query tile,
the ascending union of its rows' selections and a per-row bitmask over those
positions; `llm_attn_wmma.comp -DGATHER` then runs a **dense** attention over the
list — no axis walk, no block skip, no `blkAny` vote, and no causal comparison
anywhere. Two dispatches and not one, because the mask reads the list and a
pipeline barrier is the only handoff worth trusting between two passes over a
buffer.

Three things make it affordable, and none of them existed in P13.

**The value plane had to move.** A gathered cell's sixteen dims for one head-dim
group are 32 contiguous bytes and a selected run is four consecutive cells, so a
run is one 128-byte line — *in the key plane*. The value was stored transposed
(one dim's sixteen cells contiguous) because the reduction axis of `p.v` is the
cell and `coopMatLoad`'s ColumnMajor read the B operand straight; a run was then
four halves out of each of sixteen 32-byte rows, which is the whole tile read for
a quarter of it. RowMajor over a cell-major tile reads the **same matrix** —
element (k=cell, n=dim) at `k*16 + n` rather than `n*16 + k` — so the fix is one
line in `llm_attn_pack.comp` and one in the load, it is a permutation inside the
512-byte tile, and every exact gate stayed exact. It costs the *block* kernel
about 7% of `attn.attn` (0.9528 → 1.0236 ms a token at 128 000) and buys the
gather half its traffic; decode, which reads the same plane through P8's split
build, did not move at all.

256 dims is 16 KB of LDS, and a single-wave workgroup that takes 16 KB is four
resident per 64 KB where this kernel gets twenty. Occupancy is the one thing a
prefill cannot trade (P13-3), so the staging rides the loop that was already over
the groups: `KTIL * 256` halves, 1 KB at the shipped rung, double-buffered so the
next group's global loads overlap the current group's matrix ops.

bits it writes, so the loop has one predicate where the block kernel had three,
and the row max loses its `break`.

| gathered `qt1_kt4` | 0.4512 | 0.5940 |
| the gather's own two dispatches | 0.0144 | 0.0228 |

linear in the cells it visits and nothing else, which is the third time that has
been the answer (P13-2 predicted 1.49x from a cell count and measured 1.46x).

agreeing to 0.3%.

P13 took the narrow 16-cell block because at depth the kernel was short of cells

width is decided by reuse again — which is the ladder L2f measured before depth
was in the picture. 32 cells wins: `qt1_kt1` gives up a cooperative-matrix tile
of reuse and leaves half the lanes idle in the staging loop, and `qt1_kt4` doubles
the LDS and the per-chunk register pressure for nothing.

**The gather is the first kernel in this vertical that is not chunk-invariant,
and unlike P8's split it cannot be made so.** L7a's gate is that a token at cell

every ladder here holds it: a rung tiles the same arithmetic differently, P7's
skip drops blocks that contribute nothing, and P8's split strides *absolute* key
blocks precisely so that a slice does not depend on how the prompt was cut.

A gathered list is the union of a query tile's sixteen rows. A chunk that ends
inside the tile has fewer rows to union, so the same absolute tile gathers a
different list, the list is partitioned into different key chunks, and the online
softmax folds its rescales in a different order. The *set* each row attends over

not associative.

~3 GB together). `-llm` and `-image` do not fit in one 128 GB process, on
purpose — so no footprint quantisation is planned for the small verticals.

**Where the work goes next.** The live item is **long-context prompt
processing**: **P13 (2026-09-22)** made a 128 000-cell prefill run at all —
the submit budget had no depth term in it, so a 2048-row pass at ~115k held
the gfx ring past P0's 2 s watchdog — and then took it from **471.7 to 563.6
tok/s** by making the attention kernel's key block 16 cells instead of 32
([`research/p13-long-context-prefill.md`](research/p13-long-context-prefill.md)).
**The target is 900 tok/s at 128k and the arithmetic now says exactly what
is left**: the floor of everything flat in depth is 0.803 ms a token, the
attention is 0.566 after P13, and the selection plus its expansion are 0.28.
The selection change and a wider ubatch reach ~700; **only the per-cell
gather reaches 900**, and it is now priced at 2.8x rather than the 4.9x it
needed before P13. Beyond that, each vertical's
list is in its own rough order of value. The context-depth regression that
stood at the head of this list is **closed** — **P7**, **P8**, **P9** and **P10**, all
2026-09-21, take decode at 64k from **4.05 to 27.69 tok/s (6.8x)** and the
falloff from depth zero from **6.9x down to 1.3x down** (0.14x → 0.79x of the
depth-zero rate). P7 was three kernels that walked the *cache* rather than
the *context* plus a QSA selection that was a mask and never a skip
([`research/p7-context-depth.md`](research/p7-context-depth.md)); **P8, P9 and P10
are one finding**

content.text: Decisive: **doubling the QK matrix work costs 2.7%** — the matrix cores are nearly free and the kernel is bound by the gather loads and the LDS round-trip. That makes sharing the staged K/V across heads the right lever. Let me build it.

input.command: cd shaders && cp /tmp/wmma.bak llm_attn_wmma.comp && grep -n "shared float stage\|shared float16_t pbuf\|shared float bcorr\|shared float rowMax\|shared float blkMax\|shared float rowSum\|shared uint selw\|shared uint blkAny\|layout(local_size_x" llm_attn_wmma.comp
input.description: Restore and locate the shared arrays

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import re
p='llm_attn_wmma.comp'
s=open(p).read()

# the lane / wave / head prologue
old='''    uint past = SEQ_PAST;
    uint n = past + pc.tokens;       // cells in the cache, keys to attend over
    uint lane = gl_LocalInvocationID.x;
    if (q0 >= pc.tokens || head >= pc.heads) {
        return;
    }'''
new='''    uint past = SEQ_PAST;
    uint n = past + pc.tokens;       // cells in the cache, keys to attend over
    uint tid = gl_LocalInvocationID.x;
#if HPW > 1
    // Each wave is a head; the workgroup shares the gather. `heads % HPW == 0`
    // is the host's promise (gathHeadsPerWG), so no wave falls off the end and
    // every barrier below is reached by all of them.
    uint wv = tid / WAVE;
    uint lane = tid % WAVE;
    head = gl_WorkGroupID.y * HPW + wv;
#else
    const uint wv = 0u;
    uint lane = tid;
#endif
    // The wave's slice of the LDS the softmax uses. Zero at HPW = 1.
    uint sBase = wv * SSTAGE, pBase = wv * SPBUF, bBase = wv * SBCORR, rBase = wv * BM;
    if (q0 >= pc.tokens || head >= pc.heads) {
        return;
    }'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)

# head is now assigned, so it cannot be declared const-initialised
s=s.replace('    uint head = gl_WorkGroupID.y;\n','    uint head = gl_WorkGroupID.y;\n',1)

reps = [
 ('    for (uint i = lane; i < BM; i += WAVE) {\n        rowMax[i] = -1.0 / 0.0;\n    }',
  '    for (uint i = lane; i < BM; i += WAVE) {\n        rowMax[rBase + i] = -1.0 / 0.0;\n    }'),
 ('coopMatStore(s[qq][kk], stage, (kk * QT + qq) * (TILE * TILE), TILE,',
  'coopMatStore(s[qq][kk], stage, sBase + (kk * QT + qq) * (TILE * TILE), TILE,'),
 ('                mx = max(mx, stage[((c / TILE) * QT + qi) * (TILE * TILE) +\n                    r * TILE + (c % TILE)]);\n            }\n            mx = subgroupClusteredMax(mx, RCL);\n            if (lane % RCL == 0u) {\n                blkMax[row] = mx;',
  '                mx = max(mx, stage[sBase + ((c / TILE) * QT + qi) * (TILE * TILE) +\n                    r * TILE + (c % TILE)]);\n            }\n            mx = subgroupClusteredMax(mx, RCL);\n            if (lane % RCL == 0u) {\n                blkMax[rBase + row] = mx;'),
 ('                mx = max(mx, stage[((c / TILE) * QT + qi) * (TILE * TILE) +\n                    r * TILE + (c % TILE)]);\n            }\n            blkMax[i] = mx;',
  '                mx = max(mx, stage[sBase + ((c / TILE) * QT + qi) * (TILE * TILE) +\n                    r * TILE + (c % TILE)]);\n            }\n            blkMax[rBase + i] = mx;'),
 ('            float mo = rowMax[i];\n            float mn = max(mo, blkMax[i]);\n            rowMax[i] = mn;',
  '            float mo = rowMax[rBase + i];\n            float mn = max(mo, blkMax[rBase + i]);\n            rowMax[rBase + i] = mn;'),
 ('                stage[qi * (TILE * TILE) + r * TILE + c] = mn;\n                bcorr[qi * (TILE * TILE) + r * TILE + c] = corr;',
  '                stage[sBase + qi * (TILE * TILE) + r * TILE + c] = mn;\n                bcorr[bBase + qi * (TILE * TILE) + r * TILE + c] = corr;'),
 ('coopMatLoad(mrow, stage, qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);\n            coopMatLoad(ccorr, bcorr, qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);',
  'coopMatLoad(mrow, stage, sBase + qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);\n            coopMatLoad(ccorr, bcorr, bBase + qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);'),
 ('coopMatStore(ACCH(p), pbuf, (qq * TILE) * BN + kk * TILE, BN,',
  'coopMatStore(ACCH(p), pbuf, pBase + (qq * TILE) * BN + kk * TILE, BN,'),
 ('            if (!selected(i / BN, i & (BN - 1u), selBit)) {\n                pbuf[i] = float16_t(0.0);',
  '            if (!selected(i / BN, i & (BN - 1u), selBit)) {\n                pbuf[pBase + i] = float16_t(0.0);'),
 ('                    (sparse && !selected(row, col, selBit))) {\n                    pbuf[i] = float16_t(0.0);',
  '                    (sparse && !selected(row, col, selBit))) {\n                    pbuf[pBase + i] = float16_t(0.0);'),
 ('coopMatLoad(fragP[qq][kk], pbuf, (qq * TILE) * BN + kk * TILE, BN,',
  'coopMatLoad(fragP[qq][kk], pbuf, pBase + (qq * TILE) * BN + kk * TILE, BN,'),
 ('        coopMatStore(lsum[qq], stage, qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE,',
  '        coopMatStore(lsum[qq], stage, sBase + qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE,'),
 ('        rowSum[i] = stage[qi * (TILE * TILE) + r * TILE];',
  '        rowSum[rBase + i] = stage[sBase + qi * (TILE * TILE) + r * TILE];'),
 ('            act[at] = rowMax[i];\n            act[at + 1u] = rowSum[i];',
  '            act[at] = rowMax[rBase + i];\n            act[at + 1u] = rowSum[rBase + i];'),
 ('            coopMatStore(o[qq][j], stage, qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE,',
  '            coopMatStore(o[qq][j], stage, sBase + qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE,'),
 ('                act[dst + c] = stage[src + c];',
  '                act[dst + c] = stage[sBase + src + c];'),
 ('            float inv = (rowSum[row] > 0.0) ? 1.0 / rowSum[row] : 0.0;',
  '            float inv = (rowSum[rBase + row] > 0.0) ? 1.0 / rowSum[rBase + row] : 0.0;'),
 ('                hact[dst + c] = float16_t(stage[src + c] * inv / (1.0 + exp(-g)));',
  '                hact[dst + c] = float16_t(stage[sBase + src + c] * inv / (1.0 + exp(-g)));'),
]
for a,b in reps:
    n = s.count(a)
    assert n >= 1, a[:70]
    s = s.replace(a,b)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("ok")

python3 - <<'PY'
p='research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='''## Where 128k stands

PLACEHOLDER: the sweep table, the ubatch, and the budget.
'''
new='''## P14-5: four things that are measured inert, and the probe that explains them

The gathered kernel is 2.15x and it is **34% of this device's matrix-core peak**,
so it looked like there was another 2x sitting in it. There is not, and four arms
say why. Each is one build, `-pp 2048 -ctx 136000 -layers 4`, `attn.attn` in ms a
token at 128 000 cells scaled to 48 layers:

| arm | `attn.attn` | |
|---|---:|---:|
| the shipped gathered kernel | 0.4524 | 1.00x |
| a subgroup staging barrier instead of a workgroup one | 0.4536 | 1.00x |
| two head-dim groups a staging barrier (`GRP=2`) | 0.4512 | 1.00x |
| four (`GRP=4`) | 0.6072 | **0.75x** |
| two query heads a workgroup, sharing the staged key (`HPW=2`) | 0.4344 | 1.04x |
| four (`HPW=4`) | 0.6012 | **0.75x** |
| **the QK matrix work, doubled** | **0.4644** | **0.97x** |

The last row is the probe and it is the whole answer. **Doubling the matrix work
costs 2.7%**, so the matrix cores are ~5% of this kernel and nothing that makes
them busier or idler will move it. The barrier arms then say the same for
latency — for the fourth time in this vertical, after P11-4's hoist, P12-4's
reduction tree and P13-3's block list: *latency that matters at decode does not
matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy.* And `HPW=2`, which halves both
the global gather reads and the LDS writes by sharing them across two query heads
of one kv head, buys **4%** — so the gather's own traffic is not the cost either.

What is left, by elimination, is the **LDS round-trip for the fragments and the
per-head softmax scaffolding**, neither of which any of these arms touches: a key
chunk reads 32 KB back out of LDS into cooperative matrices per head however it
got there, and the row max, the rescale, the exponential and the mask all run per
head over `BM x BN`. Both scale with the union, which is why the kernel's cost is
linear in the cells it visits and why 2.15x fewer cells was 2.15x.

The two knobs stay as a ladder with a measured answer (`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP`,
`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS`, both defaulting to 1) because the 0.75x arms are the
informative ones: LDS is occupancy, and this kernel is single waves that want to
be many.

## Where 128k stands

PLACEHOLDER_TABLE

## What is left

- **The union is 3.4x one row's selection** and that is the gathered kernel's
  floor, because the fragment is sixteen rows and the rows are consecutive
  tokens. 2 051 cells a row against 7 049 a tile at 128 000 cells: a per-row
  attention would do 3.4x less work and cannot use a matrix core. Nothing in
  this vertical closes that gap; it is the shape of the hardware against the
  shape of QSA.
- **The floor is now most of a prefill token at depth.** At 128 000 cells and
  ubatch 2048 the attention block is under a third of it and `moe.up` alone is a
  quarter; P11 and P12 established that the MoE prefill GEMM is bound by its
  per-tile slab unpack and that gutting the whole Q4_K scale path is only 1.21x.
- **`maxStorageBufferRange` caps the cache at about 148k cells** and now says so.
  256k needs L6a's array-of-buffers, one a layer — and the guard is what makes
  that a decision rather than a silent wrong answer.
- **`attn.gathmask` is 0.015 ms a token at 128 000 cells**, 5% of the gathered
  attention, and it is the one term here that is a scattered read by nature: the
  per-row mask over the gathered positions. It is already done once for all
  twenty-four heads and already caches the mask word across a run.
'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY

41	f32 a cache cell a token, `rows * nKV` of them, which at 128 000 cells and a

45	That tensor has `nKV/ratio + 1` distinct values in it. All `ratio` cells of a
46	pooled block carry one block score (`llm_attn_score.comp`) and every cell the

51	not computed at all.

53	`shaders/llm_attn_selblk.comp` is that kernel. Three things have to hold and all
54	three are arithmetic rather than hope:

56	1. **The threshold.** A weighted histogram over blocks counts exactly the cells
57	   the per-cell histogram counted, because every cell of block `b` has key `b`
58	   and nothing else does. The total weight is exactly `ncols`.
59	2. **The tie fill.** The reference appends cells equal to the threshold in

61	   the keys that come from blocks. Two blocks whose scores happen to be equal are

71	longer a read per cell. Cells are grouped `ratio` to a block and a word is

73	wholly past this token's position is every cell -inf with no read at all.

75	Measured — 4 layers, one full-attention layer, `-pp 2048 -ctx 136000`, scaled to
76	the 48 layers that count, with `attn.attn` and `attn.score` as the controls:
77	
78	| ms a token at 128 000 | cell select | block select | |

80	| `attn.select` | 0.2808 | **0.0204** | **13.8x** |
81	| `attn.expand` | 0.0456 | — | gone |
82	| `attn.attn` (control) | 0.9516 | 0.9528 | 1.00x |
83	| `attn.score` (control) | 0.0792 | 0.0804 | 1.00x |

86	went with it: the histogram is bounded at the last block a cell can reach, so a

89

91	30 405 462 selected cells over four chunk schedules, and the layer's own output,
92	identical to the last bit. The schedules are the point: at 4096 tokens in a

98	The old kernel stays as the control arm (`LLM_ATTN_EXPAND_CELLS=1`), which is

101	
102	## P14-2: the per-cell gather
103	
104	P13 compacted the *blocks* the selection leaves anything in and measured 1.00x.
105	The kernel it fed still read every cell of a live block, and the 2.15x between

name: a-benchmark-that-gets-faster
description: "maxStorageBufferRange is silent when exceeded — the driver clamps and the kernel reads zeros, so the run comes back FASTER and wrong. Checked by checkBufferRange since 2026-09-22."
metadata:

**A VkBuffer larger than `maxStorageBufferRange` (4 GiB - 4 here) is legal to
create; binding more of it than that at a descriptor is not, and the driver
**clamps instead of failing**. A kernel reading past the range gets zeros.**

This cost a sweep on 2026-09-22. `cmd/llm -depth` raises `-ctx` to whatever the
sweep needs, and five depths to 128 000 at `-pp 4096` needs
`128000 + 5*(4096+8) = 148520` cells — a 4.39 GB fp16 attention arena against a
4.29 GB descriptor. No crash, no warning: the deepest layers attended over a
cache of zeros, the indexer degenerated to a contiguous recent window, and the
run came back at **1124 tok/s at 128k against a true 881** — 1.28x too fast,
in the direction nobody audits.

**The tell was `SelUnion`**: a sixteen-row query tile's union read **2 063**
cells against one row's 2 051, where a healthy run reads 7 049. A selection
where every row of a tile picks the same contiguous cells is not a model
property, it is a broken cache.

`checkBufferRange` in `llm/gpu.go` is now an error on both attention arenas and
names the cell cap it computes from the cache's own geometry. **The rule this
leaves**: when a change makes a benchmark faster than the arithmetic allows,
price the kernel in FLOP/s or bytes/s against the device's peak before
believing it — the gathered attention at 128k runs at 34% of matrix-core peak,
and 1124 tok/s implied 3x over.

The **healthy** sizing: `-depths 128000 -ctx 139000` alone fits any ubatch up to
8192; a five-depth sweep only fits at `-pp 2048`. See
[[long-context-prefill-128k]], [[strix-halo-bench-runs]],
[[graphstats-kinds-aliases]].

p='research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''# P14 — the gather, and 128k prefills at PLACEHOLDER tok/s

> **PLACEHOLDER headline.**''','''# P14 — the gather, and 128k prefills past 900 tok/s

> **The target is met.** A 128 000-cell prefill runs at **826.0 tok/s** at ubatch
> 2048 against P13's 563.6 (**1.47x**), at **PLACEHOLDER_4096** at 4096, and at
> **PLACEHOLDER_8192** at 8192 — which is the 900 tok/s `GOALS.md` asked for. The
> falloff from depth zero goes **0.50x to 0.72x** at the same ubatch, and decode
> at 128k does not move (22.18 against 22.27). Four changes and **four measured
> refusals**, and the refusals are the interesting half: after the gather the
> attention kernel is bound by neither its matrix cores (doubling their work
> costs 2.7%), nor its gather traffic (halving it buys 4%), nor its barriers.''')
old='''## Where 128k stands

PLACEHOLDER_TABLE
'''
new='''## Where 128k stands

48 layers, shipped banks, `wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward,
`-pp 2048 -tg 8 -ctx 139000`, against P13's table at the same shape:

| depth | P13 pp | P14 pp | | P13 tg | P14 tg |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.29 | 29.31 |
| 32 000 | 825.8 | **915.6** | 1.11x | 25.84 | 25.80 |
| 64 000 | 719.6 | **892.1** | 1.24x | 24.68 | 24.46 |
| 96 000 | 607.9 | **832.3** | 1.37x | 23.24 | 22.80 |
| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.94 | 22.18 |

The falloff from depth zero is **0.72x** where P13 left it at 0.50x and P0 could
not reach the depth at all. **Decode is the control and does not move**: the
gather is prefill's kernel, P14-1's select is bit-identical, and P14-3's score is
a rounding away.

And against the **ubatch**, at 128 000 cells alone (two runs each; `-ctx 139000`
has room for any of these at one depth, and for none but 2048 across five):

| ubatch | pp tok/s at 128 000 | decode |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 826.0 | 22.18 |
| 4096 (the shipped `-llm-batch`) | **PLACEHOLDER_4096** | PLACEHOLDER_D4096 |
| 8192 | **PLACEHOLDER_8192** | PLACEHOLDER_D8192 |

That is P12's trade at depth and it is the same trade: a wider ubatch buys the
flat floor and costs decode, so 8192 is a batch summariser's setting and 4096
stays the interactive default.

Where a prefill token goes at 128 000 cells and ubatch 2048, against P13's
budget (ms a token):

	                    P13      P14

input.content:
---
name: long-context-prefill-128k
description: "Prefill against depth out to 128k after P14 (2026-09-22): 826 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and past 900 at 8192, the four changes, the four measured refusals, and the fast 4-layer probe."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

**128 000 cells prefills at 826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and PLACEHOLDER_8192 at
8192 — `GOALS.md`'s 900 is met.** P13 left it at 563.6. 48 layers, shipped banks,
`wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward, `-tg 8 -ctx 139000`. Write-up
`research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md`.

| depth | P13 pp | P14 pp | | decode |
|------:|-------:|-------:|----:|-------:|
| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.31 |
| 32 000 | 825.8 | 915.6 | 1.11x | 25.80 |
| 64 000 | 719.6 | 892.1 | 1.24x | 24.46 |
| 96 000 | 607.9 | 832.3 | 1.37x | 22.80 |
| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.18 |

Falloff from depth zero **0.50x → 0.72x**. Against the ubatch at 128 000 alone
(two runs each): 826.0 at 2048, PLACEHOLDER_4096 at 4096 (the shipped
`-llm-batch`), **PLACEHOLDER_8192 at 8192** — P12's trade at depth, so 8192 is a
batch summariser's setting. **Decode is the control and did not move.**

**Four changes.**

1. **The selection runs over block scores, not the expanded per-cell tensor**
   (`llm_attn_selblk.comp`). All `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score,
   so a weighted select over `nKV/ratio` entries is the same threshold, ties and
   bitmask. `attn.select` 0.281 → **0.020** (13.8x), `attn.expand` deleted, and
   **1.14 GB of arena** freed at ubatch 2048. Bit-identical, gated by
   `TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect` over four chunk schedules.
2. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather** (`llm_attn_gather.comp` +
   `llm_attn_wmma.comp -DGATHER`). Per query tile, the union of its rows'
   selections compacted ascending, with the causal test folded into a per-row
   mask over the gathered positions. `attn.attn` 1.024 → **0.454** (2.15x on the
   4-layer probe; 0.566 → 0.303 at 48 layers). **The value plane had to become
   cell-major first** — a selected run is `ratio` consecutive cells, one
   128-byte line, where transposed it was four halves out of sixteen rows. That
   costs the block kernel ~7% and decode nothing.
3. **The indexer's score on the matrix cores** (`llm_attn_score_wmma.comp`). It
   is a GEMM per indexer head with a rectifier: 0.077 → **0.034**. Chunk-invariant
   (a matrix product's rows are independent), and *nearer* llama.cpp's selection
   than the scalar kernel (9760 vs 9762 of 6 298 621).
4. **`checkBufferRange`** — see [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]].

**The gather is the first kernel here that is not chunk-invariant and cannot be
made so.** Its list is the union of a query tile's sixteen rows, so a chunk
ending inside the tile gathers a different list and the online softmax folds the
same terms in a different order. It is off under `Graph.PinSchedule` with the
other reassociating kernels, and the chunk-equality gates pin it (`SetGather`).
A prompt prefilled twice at the same ubatch is still bit-identical; only changing
the ubatch moves the last places. Gates: `TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells`
(exact on the set), `TestAttnGPUGatherIsTheBlockKernel` (4.1e-06 rms against
9.9e-04 from llama.cpp), `TestAttnGPUGatherRungsAgree`,
`TestAttnGPUGatherIsDispatched`.

**The union is the number that prices all of this, and P13's estimate of it was
wrong.** `AttnGPU.SelUnion` measures it: at 128 000 cells a 16-row tile reads
**15 145** cells where its rows' union is **7 049** and one row selects 2 051.
The gather is therefore 2.15x, not the 3.3x P13 projected, and the 3.4x between
the union and one row is the floor a 16-row fragment cannot reach.

**What the gathered kernel is bound by, by elimination** — four arms, all
1.00x-ish, in [[prefill-rates]]: not the matrix cores (doubling their work costs
2.7%), not the barriers, not the gather's own traffic (sharing it across two
heads buys 4%). It is the LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head
softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union.

**The fast loop is still `-depth ... -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm** — and it
**overstates** `attn.attn` because its one attention layer is denser than the
48-layer mean (19.0% live at bm16/bn16 against 11.7%). Ratios reproduce;
absolutes do not.

    /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4

**Control arms**: `LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_KERNEL=qt1_kt1|qt1_kt4`,

what `Cells()` needs), `LLM_ATTN_SCORE=scalar`.

name: long-context-prefill-128k
description: "Prefill against depth out to 128k after P14 (2026-09-22): 826 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and past 900 at 8192, the four changes, the four measured refusals, and the fast 4-layer probe."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  modified: 2026-09-22T11:38:44.739Z

**128 000 cells prefills at 826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and PLACEHOLDER_8192 at
8192 — `GOALS.md`'s 900 is met.** P13 left it at 563.6. 48 layers, shipped banks,
`wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward, `-tg 8 -ctx 139000`. Write-up
`research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md`.

| depth | P13 pp | P14 pp | | decode |
|------:|-------:|-------:|----:|-------:|
| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.31 |
| 32 000 | 825.8 | 915.6 | 1.11x | 25.80 |
| 64 000 | 719.6 | 892.1 | 1.24x | 24.46 |
| 96 000 | 607.9 | 832.3 | 1.37x | 22.80 |
| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.18 |

Falloff from depth zero **0.50x → 0.72x**. Against the ubatch at 128 000 alone
(two runs each): 826.0 at 2048, PLACEHOLDER_4096 at 4096 (the shipped
`-llm-batch`), **PLACEHOLDER_8192 at 8192** — P12's trade at depth, so 8192 is a
batch summariser's setting. **Decode is the control and did not move.**

**Four changes.**

1. **The selection runs over block scores, not the expanded per-cell tensor**
   (`llm_attn_selblk.comp`). All `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score,
   so a weighted select over `nKV/ratio` entries is the same threshold, ties and
   bitmask. `attn.select` 0.281 → **0.020** (13.8x), `attn.expand` deleted, and
   **1.14 GB of arena** freed at ubatch 2048. Bit-identical, gated by
   `TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect` over four chunk schedules.
2. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather** (`llm_attn_gather.comp` +
   `llm_attn_wmma.comp -DGATHER`). Per query tile, the union of its rows'
   selections compacted ascending, with the causal test folded into a per-row
   mask over the gathered positions. `attn.attn` 1.024 → **0.454** (2.15x on the
   4-layer probe; 0.566 → 0.303 at 48 layers). **The value plane had to become
   cell-major first** — a selected run is `ratio` consecutive cells, one
   128-byte line, where transposed it was four halves out of sixteen rows. That
   costs the block kernel ~7% and decode nothing.
3. **The indexer's score on the matrix cores** (`llm_attn_score_wmma.comp`). It
   is a GEMM per indexer head with a rectifier: 0.077 → **0.034**. Chunk-invariant
   (a matrix product's rows are independent), and *nearer* llama.cpp's selection
   than the scalar kernel (9760 vs 9762 of 6 298 621).
4. **`checkBufferRange`** — see [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]].

**The gather is the first kernel here that is not chunk-invariant and cannot be
made so.** Its list is the union of a query tile's sixteen rows, so a chunk
ending inside the tile gathers a different list and the online softmax folds the
same terms in a different order. It is off under `Graph.PinSchedule` with the
other reassociating kernels, and the chunk-equality gates pin it (`SetGather`).
A prompt prefilled twice at the same ubatch is still bit-identical; only changing
the ubatch moves the last places. Gates: `TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells`
(exact on the set), `TestAttnGPUGatherIsTheBlockKernel` (4.1e-06 rms against
9.9e-04 from llama.cpp), `TestAttnGPUGatherRungsAgree`,
`TestAttnGPUGatherIsDispatched`.

**The union is the number that prices all of this, and P13's estimate of it was
wrong.** `AttnGPU.SelUnion` measures it: at 128 000 cells a 16-row tile reads
**15 145** cells where its rows' union is **7 049** and one row selects 2 051.
The gather is therefore 2.15x, not the 3.3x P13 projected, and the 3.4x between
the union and one row is the floor a 16-row fragment cannot reach.

**What the gathered kernel is bound by, by elimination** — four arms, all
1.00x-ish, in [[prefill-rates]]: not the matrix cores (doubling their work costs
2.7%), not the barriers, not the gather's own traffic (sharing it across two
heads buys 4%). It is the LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head
softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union.

**The fast loop is still `-depth ... -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm** — and it
**overstates** `attn.attn` because its one attention layer is denser than the
48-layer mean (19.0% live at bm16/bn16 against 11.7%). Ratios reproduce;
absolutes do not.

    /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4

what `Cells()` needs), `LLM_ATTN_SCORE=scalar`.

content.content: 106:| [P13](p13-long-context-prefill.md) | **128k completes, and the attention kernel's key block was twice as wide as it should have been.** A 128 000-cell prefill **runs**, for the first time in this vertical, at **471.7 tok/s** — and the thing stopping it was never `DispatchMultiMarked`'s marks, it was that **P0's submit budget had no depth term in it**. Every measurement behind P0's `322 us a dispatch + 582 ns a dispatch-row` was taken from cell zero, so `batchFor(rows)` went on handing back the same 660 dispatches at 2048 rows whether the cache was empty or held 128 000 cells; at 64 000 those 660 already held the gfx ring for ~1.53 s of the 2 s watchdog while the budget believed it was spending 0.86, and at ~115 000 they cross it. The missing term is **10.46 ns per (row, cell)** — read straight off P12's own ladder, 1.696 s a pass at depth zero against 3.067 at 64 000 — and **only the attention dispatches carry it**, because every other block is flat in depth (P11-5). So the chunker walks the recorded sequence and cuts where the *accumulated* prediction reaches the budget, charging each dispatch what its own label costs, and rescales itself against what the last submit actually measured — **upwards only**, because the affine constant is an order out at one row and a scale that learned from decode steps would hand the next prefill four times its budget. Then **the rung**: L2f chose `qt1_kt2` on 512-token prefills from cell zero, where a 32-cell key block is two cooperative-matrix tiles of reuse against one. At depth that is the wrong ladder — what the kernel can skip is a (query tile, key block) pair, so the cost is the *union* of sixteen adjacent queries' selections at the block's width, and P11-7's own table says 11.7% of the axis at 16 cells against 17.4% at 32. The new `qt1_kt1` build is **1.61x on `attn.attn` at 128 000 cells** (0.9107 → 0.5659 ms a token), 1.60x at 96 000, 1.36x at 64 000 and 1.19x at 32 000, with `attn.select`, `attn.score` and `attn.expand` identical to three decimals as the control — **471.7 → 563.6 tok/s**, falloff 0.42x → 0.50x, two passes agreeing to 0.05-0.2%. That is P11-7's 1.40x collected as a **rung** after P11-7 lost 1.18x trying to collect it as a branch, and it is the rule that file drew, applied: change the loop's granularity, not what happens inside it. It is **prefill's rung and not decode's** — with it on both, decode at 128k went 22.94 → 22.27, because a decode step costs one wave's serial walk (P8) and halving the block doubles the walk. **The refusal is the idea that looked best going in.** `llm_attn_blocks.comp` compacts the live key blocks into an ascending per-query-tile list so the kernel iterates the list instead of the axis — bit-identical, gated as an equality, deleting **83% of the visits** at 128 000 cells for 0.001 ms a token — and it is **1.00x at every depth**, and 1.05x *against* at the narrow rung where there are twice as many dead blocks to skip. The mask read was never the cost: the same sixteen lines serve all twenty-four heads and the MALL holds the tile's whole 128 KB. Third instance of one rule, now the engine's rather than any kernel's: *latency and redundant reads that matter at decode do not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy* — 3072 single-wave workgroups against a decode step's 24. It ships behind `LLM_ATTN_BLOCK_LIST=1` because the decode split and a per-cell gather both want it. **And the arithmetic of 900 tok/s at 128k is now closed-form**: the floor of everything flat in depth is 0.803 ms a token, `attn.attn` is 0.566, and `attn.select` + `attn.expand` are 0.284 and are one change; those plus a 4096 ubatch reach ~700, and **only the per-cell gather reaches 900** — priced at 2.8x on `attn.attn` where before P13 it needed 4.9x. |

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='research/README.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='| [P13](p13-long-context-prefill.md) |'
new='''| [P14](p14-prefill-at-depth.md) | **The gather, and 128k prefills past 900 tok/s — the target met.** A 128 000-cell prefill goes from P13's **563.6** to **826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048** (1.47x, falloff from depth zero 0.50x → 0.72x) and to **PLACEHOLDER_8192 at 8192**, with decode unmoved as the control. Four changes. **The selection runs over block scores, not cells**: all `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score, so a radix select over `nKV/ratio` entries with a per-block *weight* — how many of its cells this token can see, which is closed form — reaches the same threshold, the same tie fill and the same bitmask, and `llm_attn_expand.comp` is then not computed at all. `attn.select` **0.281 → 0.020 ms a token** (13.8x, not the 4x the traffic argument predicts: the histogram is bounded at the last block a cell can reach and the 16 KB LDS cache now holds `ratio` times as many cells), the expansion deleted, and **1.14 GB of arena** freed — bit-identical over four chunk schedules, including the ones that make the incomplete tail and the causal boundary inside a partly visible block both live. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather**: per query tile, the union of its rows\' selections compacted ascending with the causal test folded into a per-row mask, then a *dense* attention over the list with no axis walk, no block skip and no causal comparison. **2.15x on `attn.attn`**, which is exactly the cell ratio — 15 145 cells read against a 7 049-cell union, measured with a new `SelUnion` instrument after P13\'s own estimate of both numbers turned out wrong. It needed **the value plane to become cell-major** first (a selected run is `ratio` consecutive cells, one 128-byte line; transposed it was four halves out of each of sixteen rows), which costs the block kernel 7% and decode nothing, and it stages one head-dim group at a time through 1 KB of LDS because occupancy is the one thing a prefill cannot trade. It is **the first kernel here that is not chunk-invariant and cannot be made so** — its list is the union of sixteen rows, so a chunk ending inside the tile folds the same terms in a different order — so it is pinned off under `PinSchedule` with the other reassociating kernels and gated by an *exact* equality on the set plus a tolerance on the answer (4.1e-06 rms against 9.9e-04 from llama.cpp). **The indexer\'s score moves to the matrix cores**, a GEMM per head with a rectifier: 0.077 → 0.034, chunk-invariant, and marginally nearer llama.cpp\'s own selection than the scalar kernel it replaces. **And `maxStorageBufferRange` gets an error instead of a comment**, because it is silent when exceeded: the driver clamps the descriptor rather than failing, so a five-depth sweep at ubatch 4096 raised `-ctx` past the cap, attended over a cache of zeros, and came back **1124 tok/s against a true 886** — 1.28x too fast, with a degenerate indexer selecting a contiguous window. *The failure mode is a benchmark that gets faster.* **Four measured refusals, and together they say what the gathered kernel is bound by**: doubling its matrix work costs **2.7%**, a subgroup staging barrier instead of a workgroup one is 1.00x, staging two head-dim groups a barrier is 1.00x (four is 0.75x), and sharing the staged key and value across two query heads of one kv head — halving both the global gather reads and the LDS writes — is **1.04x** (four heads is 0.75x). Not the matrix cores, not latency, not the gather\'s traffic: what is left is the LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union, which is why the cost is linear in the cells visited. |
| [P13](p13-long-context-prefill.md) |'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY

1	---
2	name: long-context-prefill-128k
3	description: "Prefill against depth out to 128k after P14 (2026-09-22): 826 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and past 900 at 8192, the four changes, the four measured refusals, and the fast 4-layer probe."
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 80f71c47-a621-4724-a77a-e285f8d84b61
8	  modified: 2026-09-22T11:38:44.739Z
9	---
10	
11	**128 000 cells prefills at 826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946.1 at
12	8192 — `GOALS.md`'s 900 is met.** P13 left it at 563.6. 48 layers, shipped banks,
13	`wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward, `-tg 8 -ctx 139000`. Write-up
14	`research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md`.
15	
16	| depth | P13 pp | P14 pp | | decode |
17	|------:|-------:|-------:|----:|-------:|
18	| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.31 |
19	| 32 000 | 825.8 | 915.6 | 1.11x | 25.80 |
20	| 64 000 | 719.6 | 892.1 | 1.24x | 24.46 |
21	| 96 000 | 607.9 | 832.3 | 1.37x | 22.80 |
22	| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.18 |
23	
24	Falloff from depth zero **0.50x → 0.72x**. Against the ubatch at 128 000 alone
25	(two runs each): 826.0 at 2048, 886.1 at 4096 (the shipped
26	`-llm-batch`), **946.1 at 8192** — P12's trade at depth, so 8192 is a
27	batch summariser's setting. **Decode is the control and did not move.**
28	
29	**Four changes.**
30	
31	1. **The selection runs over block scores, not the expanded per-cell tensor**
32	   (`llm_attn_selblk.comp`). All `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score,
33	   so a weighted select over `nKV/ratio` entries is the same threshold, ties and
34	   bitmask. `attn.select` 0.281 → **0.020** (13.8x), `attn.expand` deleted, and
35	   **1.14 GB of arena** freed at ubatch 2048. Bit-identical, gated by
36	   `TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect` over four chunk schedules.
37	2. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather** (`llm_attn_gather.comp` +
38	   `llm_attn_wmma.comp -DGATHER`). Per query tile, the union of its rows'
39	   selections compacted ascending, with the causal test folded into a per-row
40	   mask over the gathered positions. `attn.attn` 1.024 → **0.454** (2.15x on the
41	   4-layer probe; 0.566 → 0.303 at 48 layers). **The value plane had to become
42	   cell-major first** — a selected run is `ratio` consecutive cells, one
43	   128-byte line, where transposed it was four halves out of sixteen rows. That
44	   costs the block kernel ~7% and decode nothing.
45	3. **The indexer's score on the matrix cores** (`llm_attn_score_wmma.comp`). It
46	   is a GEMM per indexer head with a rectifier: 0.077 → **0.034**. Chunk-invariant
47	   (a matrix product's rows are independent), and *nearer* llama.cpp's selection
48	   than the scalar kernel (9760 vs 9762 of 6 298 621).
49	4. **`checkBufferRange`** — see [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]].
50	
51	**The gather is the first kernel here that is not chunk-invariant and cannot be
52	made so.** Its list is the union of a query tile's sixteen rows, so a chunk
53	ending inside the tile gathers a different list and the online softmax folds the
54	same terms in a different order. It is off under `Graph.PinSchedule` with the
55	other reassociating kernels, and the chunk-equality gates pin it (`SetGather`).
56	A prompt prefilled twice at the same ubatch is still bit-identical; only changing
57	the ubatch moves the last places. Gates: `TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells`
58	(exact on the set), `TestAttnGPUGatherIsTheBlockKernel` (4.1e-06 rms against
59	9.9e-04 from llama.cpp), `TestAttnGPUGatherRungsAgree`,
60	`TestAttnGPUGatherIsDispatched`.
61	
62	**The union is the number that prices all of this, and P13's estimate of it was
63	wrong.** `AttnGPU.SelUnion` measures it: at 128 000 cells a 16-row tile reads
64	**15 145** cells where its rows' union is **7 049** and one row selects 2 051.
65	The gather is therefore 2.15x, not the 3.3x P13 projected, and the 3.4x between
66	the union and one row is the floor a 16-row fragment cannot reach.
67	
68	**What the gathered kernel is bound by, by elimination** — four arms, all
69	1.00x-ish, in [[prefill-rates]]: not the matrix cores (doubling their work costs
70	2.7%), not the barriers, not the gather's own traffic (sharing it across two
71	heads buys 4%). It is the LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head
72	softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union.
73	
74	**The fast loop is still `-depth ... -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm** — and it
75	**overstates** `attn.attn` because its one attention layer is denser than the
76	48-layer mean (19.0% live at bm16/bn16 against 11.7%). Ratios reproduce;
77	absolutes do not.
78	
79	    /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4
80	
81	**Control arms**: `LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_KERNEL=qt1_kt1|qt1_kt4`,
82	`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS`, `LLM_ATTN_EXPAND_CELLS=1` (also
83	what `Cells()` needs), `LLM_ATTN_SCORE=scalar`.
84	
85	See [[prefill-rates]], [[context-depth-rates]], [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]],
86	[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
87	[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[graphstats-kinds-aliases]].

# P14 — the gather, and 128k prefills past 900 tok/s

> **The target is met.** A 128 000-cell prefill runs at **826.0 tok/s** at ubatch
> 2048 against P13's 563.6 (**1.47x**), at **886.1** at 4096, and at
> **946.1** at 8192 — which is the 900 tok/s `GOALS.md` asked for. The
> falloff from depth zero goes **0.50x to 0.72x** at the same ubatch, and decode
> at 128k does not move (22.18 against 22.27). Four changes and **four measured
> refusals**, and the refusals are the interesting half: after the gather the
> attention kernel is bound by neither its matrix cores (doubling their work
> costs 2.7%), nor its gather traffic (halving it buys 4%), nor its barriers.

...
| 32 000 | 825.8 | **915.6** | 1.11x | 25.84 | 25.80 |
| 64 000 | 719.6 | **892.1** | 1.24x | 24.68 | 24.46 |
| 96 000 | 607.9 | **832.3** | 1.37x | 23.24 | 22.80 |
| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.94 | 22.18 |

The falloff from depth zero is **0.72x** where P13 left it at 0.50x and P0 could
not reach the depth at all. **Decode is the control and does not move**: the
gather is prefill's kernel, P14-1's select is bit-identical, and P14-3's score is
a rounding away.

And against the **ubatch**, at 128 000 cells alone (two runs each; `-ctx 139000`
has room for any of these at one depth, and for none but 2048 across five):

| ubatch | pp tok/s at 128 000 | decode |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 826.0 | 22.18 |
| 4096 (the shipped `-llm-batch`) | **886.1** | 20.74 |
| 8192 | **946.1** | 18.48 |

That is P12's trade at depth and it is the same trade: a wider ubatch buys the
flat floor and costs decode, so 8192 is a batch summariser's setting and 4096
stays the interactive default.

budget (ms a token):

	attn.attn          0.566    0.303     the gather
	attn.select        0.233    0.021     the block select
	attn.score         0.078    0.034     the matrix cores

content.text:
I have everything but the whole-package regression run, which is still executing. Here's where it landed.

## 900 tok/s at 128k — met, at 946.1

48 layers, shipped banks, `wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward, two runs each:

| depth | P13 | **P14** | | decode |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.31 |
| 32 000 | 825.8 | **915.6** | 1.11x | 25.80 |
| 64 000 | 719.6 | **892.1** | 1.24x | 24.46 |
| 96 000 | 607.9 | **832.3** | 1.37x | 22.80 |
| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.18 |

Against the ubatch at 128k: 826.0 at 2048, **886.1** at 4096 (the shipped `-llm-batch`), **946.1** at 8192 (946.7/945.4, reproducible to 0.14%). Falloff from depth zero 0.50x → 0.72x. Decode is the control and did not move.

## Four changes

1. **The selection runs over block scores, not the expanded per-cell tensor.** All `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score, so a weighted radix select over `nKV/ratio` entries reaches the same threshold, tie fill and bitmask. `attn.select` **0.281 → 0.020** ms/token (13.8x), `attn.expand` deleted, **1.14 GB of arena** freed. Bit-identical over 30.4M selected cells and four chunk schedules.
2. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather** — the union of a query tile's rows' selections, compacted, with the causal test folded into a per-row mask. **2.15x on `attn.attn`**, exactly the cell ratio. It needed the value plane to become cell-major first.
3. **The indexer's score on the matrix cores** (a GEMM per head with a rectifier): 0.077 → 0.034, and marginally *nearer* llama.cpp's selection than the scalar kernel.
4. **`checkBufferRange`** — see below.

## Two things you should know

**The gather is the first kernel here that isn't chunk-invariant, and can't be made so.** Its list is the union of sixteen rows, so a chunk ending inside a tile folds the same terms in a different order. It's pinned off under `PinSchedule` with the other reassociating kernels; a prompt prefilled twice at the same ubatch is still bit-identical, and only changing the ubatch moves the last places. Gated exactly on the *set* and by tolerance on the answer (4.1e-06 rms against 9.9e-04 from llama.cpp).

**A sweep I ran came back 1.28x too fast and wrong.** `maxStorageBufferRange` is silent when exceeded — the driver clamps the descriptor instead of failing, so the deep layers attended over a cache of zeros and the indexer degenerated to a contiguous window. `checkBufferRange` now errors on both attention arenas. The failure mode is a benchmark that gets *faster*, which is the direction nobody audits; I only caught it by pricing the kernel against matrix-core peak.

## Four measured refusals

Doubling the gathered kernel's matrix work costs **2.7%**; a subgroup staging barrier is 1.00x; staging two head-dim groups a barrier is 1.00x (four is 0.75x); sharing the staged K/V across two query heads — halving both the global gather reads and the LDS writes — is **1.04x** (four is 0.75x). So it's not the matrix cores, not latency, not the gather's traffic. What's left is the LDS round-trip and the per-head softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union — which is why cost is linear in cells visited, and why 2.15x fewer cells was 2.15x.

Write-up in `research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md`; `TODO.md`, the research index and memory are updated. All attention and graph gates pass individually (including `TestGraphIsAChunkSplit` and `TestAttnGPURungsAgree`); the full-package `go test ./llm/` run over the blocks I didn't touch is still in flight and I'll flag it if anything falls over.

---
name: llm-test-suite-gotchas
description: "Three ways go test ./llm/ misleads: Go's 10-minute default timeout, a TestGraphLogits failure that is pre-existing on main, and a relative LLM_BANK_CACHE writing 23 GB into llm/."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d77f87a5-b722-4ac5-aaa9-d322f713f1da
  modified: 2026-09-21T22:34:36.040Z
---

**`go test ./llm/` needs `-timeout 60m`.** Go's default is ten minutes and the
suite runs past it inside `TestQSASelectionSurvivesOurScores`. What you get is
a panic stack and `FAIL strix-halo-vulkan/llm 600.024s`, which **reads as a
real failure and is not one**. With a warm bank cache the whole suite is
~180 s; cold it is much longer.

**`TestGraphLogits` fails on `main` (checked 2026-09-21, fdb5bcd).** It wants
ten of ten top tokens against the llama.cpp reference dump and gets nine —
argmax still agrees (561), and the divergence is the rank-9/10 tail
(`220` against `15767`). Before blaming a change for it, `git stash` and
re-run: the base prints *byte-identical* diagnostics
(`maxAbs 2.507e+00 at 141557`, `rms 5.148e-01`, the same top-10 list).

**That identity is also the cheapest whole-model bit-exactness check there
is.** A change that claims to be bit-exact should reproduce those numbers to
the digit through all 48 layers — stronger than any block test, and it costs
one 61 s run.

**`LLM_BANK_CACHE` is a relative path, and `go test ./llm/` resolves it
against `llm/`.** So exporting the usual
`LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache` and running the
tests silently builds a **23 GB** duplicate at `llm/models/`, untracked. Use
an absolute path, or `rm -rf llm/models` afterwards. The real cache
(26 GB, 199 files) is at the repo root.

**How to apply:** the useful per-change gates are
`go test ./llm/ -run 'TestAttn|TestMoEGPU|TestGraphIsAChunkSplit' -timeout 30m`
(~80 s), and run the full suite only when something broad moved. See
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

a panic stack and `FAIL strix-halo-vulkan/llm 600.024s`, which **reads as a
real failure and is not one**. With a warm bank cache the whole suite is
~180 s; cold it is much longer.

**`TestGraphLogits` fails on `main` (checked 2026-09-21, fdb5bcd).** It wants
ten of ten top tokens against the llama.cpp reference dump and gets nine —
argmax still agrees (561), and the divergence is the rank-9/10 tail
(`220` against `15767`). Before blaming a change for it, `git stash` and
re-run: the base prints *byte-identical* diagnostics
(`maxAbs 2.507e+00 at 141557`, `rms 5.148e-01`, the same top-10 list).

**That identity is also the cheapest whole-model bit-exactness check there
is.** A change that claims to be bit-exact should reproduce those numbers to
the digit through all 48 layers — stronger than any block test, and it costs
one 61 s run.

**`LLM_BANK_CACHE` is a relative path, and `go test ./llm/` resolves it
against `llm/`.** So exporting the usual
`LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache` and running the
tests silently builds a **23 GB** duplicate at `llm/models/`, untracked. Use
an absolute path, or `rm -rf llm/models` afterwards. The real cache
(26 GB, 199 files) is at the repo root.

**How to apply:** the useful per-change gates are
`go test ./llm/ -run 'TestAttn|TestMoEGPU|TestGraphIsAChunkSplit' -timeout 30m`
(~80 s), and run the full suite only when something broad moved. See
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

content.text:
Done. The suite verdict closes it out.

## `go test ./llm/` — one failure, and it's the known one

`TestGraphLogits` is the only failure, and it fails on `main` for a reason that predates this work (nine of ten top tokens, argmax agreeing). What matters is that its diagnostics came back **byte-identical to the base** — `maxAbs 2.507e+00 at 141557`, `rms 5.148e-01`, the same top-ten list — through all 48 layers. That's the cheapest whole-model bit-exactness check in the repo, and it confirms the three changes that claim bit-exactness (the block select, the value plane's new layout, the arena changes) all at once.

I also walked into a trap my own notes warn about: `LLM_BANK_CACHE` is relative and `go test ./llm/` resolves it against `llm/`, so the run built a 23 GB duplicate cache at `llm/models`. Removed.

## Final state

**128 000 cells: 826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048, 886.1 at 4096, 946.1 at 8192** — against P13's 563.6. Falloff from depth zero 0.50x → 0.72x. Decode unmoved (22.18 vs 22.27).

Four changes: the selection over block scores (13.8x on `attn.select`, expansion deleted, 1.14 GB of arena freed); the per-cell gather (2.15x on `attn.attn`, needing the value plane to become cell-major); the indexer's score on the matrix cores (2.3x); and `checkBufferRange`.

Two things worth carrying forward:

- **The gather trades an invariant.** It's the first kernel here that isn't chunk-invariant and can't be made so, so it's pinned off under `PinSchedule`. A prompt prefilled twice at the same ubatch is still bit-identical; only changing the ubatch moves the last places.
- **The remaining headroom is real but not where I'd have guessed.** The gathered kernel is at 34% of matrix-core peak, and all four candidate bounds are eliminated by measurement — doubling its matrix work costs 2.7%, halving its gather traffic buys 4%. What's left is the LDS round-trip and the per-head softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union, and the union is 3.4x one row's selection because the fragment is sixteen rows. That gap is the shape of the hardware against the shape of QSA.

`research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md` has the full write-up; `TODO.md`, the research index and memory are updated.
